methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Fairfax City Business Leaders Tell Spanberger About Rising Costs, AI, Workforce Challenges - Patch
signals.signal_reading: Business leaders in Fairfax discussing AI as a strategic workforce challenge signals deep engagement with AI transformation in NoVA's already-concentrated tech ecosystem, reinforcing metro advantages in navigating AI transitions while rural regions face these challenges without organized business infrastructure.

signals.title: AI pressure grows on Richmond's young workforce - Axios
signals.signal_reading: AI creating 'pressure' on Richmond's young workforce suggests platform-delivered automation affecting entry-level work broadly rather than building deep AI capabilities, pointing toward shallow adoption that reshapes labor markets without creating new technical capacity.

signals.title: Virginia Beach schools bring ChatGPT under division oversight as AI use grows - 13newsnow.com
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Beach schools bringing ChatGPT under oversight represents managed shallow adoption—institutions regulating consumer AI tools rather than building indigenous AI development capacity, distributing access but not depth.

signals.title: Norfolk could get AI assist for non-emergency calls - WAVY.com
signals.signal_reading: Norfolk deploying AI for non-emergency call handling exemplifies procurement-based shallow adoption where municipalities consume vendor solutions rather than develop local AI expertise, distributing utility without building technical capability.

signals.title: How one Virginia county’s AI platform protects sensitive data - Route Fifty
signals.signal_reading: A Virginia county developing its own AI platform with data protection features signals movement toward distributed deep capability—local government building rather than buying AI solutions suggests technical capacity spreading beyond traditional tech hubs into county-level implementation.
